answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring a trellis of real interdependent work before granting privileges: each completed task for an established peer leaves a relic — a hashed deliverable anyone can re-verify — plus a single-use service credit that can never be recycled between identities. The honest signal is the density of this work graph. Faking one identity is cheap, but forging a trellis costs real labor per fake, since every credit needs a counterparty staking their own standing on the work quality, so a Sybil army cost scales with effort, not account count.
